# ASU 2026 Official Template — Google Slides Presentation Source V1

**Date:** 2026-10-13
**Applies to:** User-requested ASU-branded MSE-thesis Google Slides presentations, including the distinct **10-slide October 2026 presentation**. Does not silently change the separate canonical Deck3 **8-slide/3-minute** master, historical 13/14-slide Chapter I variants, scientific evidence, or a frozen goal/objective.

## Source of template truth
- **Provided official template:** user-uploaded `thesis.pptx`, headed `2026 Official ASU presentation template`; from ASU Enterprise Brand Strategy and Management, as asserted within the user-provided template.
- **Raw source SHA-256:** `22a7b136870223ac7cc6daf283ceed9d489da0cba382fae689267f90fc3aa2e6`.
- **Inspected:** 19 instructional/sample slides, 16:9 (10.0 x 5.625 in), 122 PowerPoint layouts, with ASU-branded opening slide, agenda, content, statistics, two-column and closing layouts. The template explicitly states access is limited to `asu.edu` email addresses and provides closed-caption placement/safe-zone instructions.
- **External university authority:** https://brandguide.asu.edu/execution-guidelines/presentations (ASU recommends the native Google Slides collaboration/workflow).
- **Rights handling:** A user-provided institutional template is used for that user's requested deck. **Do not commit/distribute the 2026 ASU PPTX binary, extracted brand assets, or template photographs to a public repository.** Keep them in approved user Drive/authorized institutional channels. Link to the presentation does not grant public access.

## Binding routing for future ASU thesis requests

1. **If user says official ASU template / ASU MSE Google Slides:** inspect the supplied 2026 ASU PPTX or an authorized native ASU Google Slides template. Reuse its actual master/layouts. Do **not** imitate ASU branding from scratch.
2. **Use native Google Slides as the presentation workspace** whenever connected and authorized; create/copy an editable derivative, never overwrite the read-only ASU template or alter a Google Drive original except when explicitly authorized. Keep text, citations, equations, and connectors as native elements. Do not assume PowerPoint-to-Slides conversion is 100% lossless.
3. **Read the variant's source text:** 10-slide content at `thesis/presentations/deck3/ASU_2026_MSE_THESIS_TEN_SLIDE_CONTENT_V1.md`; do not impose 8-slide, 13-slide or 14-slide content onto this distinct deck.
4. **ASU caption-safe content:** inspect the official template's 2026 green safe zone / red caption overlay exclusion before placing any text important to the live audience. Keep critical copy away from live closed-caption overlays.
5. **Scientific controls win:** 2026 thesis title, current main-branch V1 objective language until V2 PR #76 is merged; eight working components P1-P4 / T1-T4; external heat H(t) common forcing; independently unqualified P→T_e/T_e→P mechanisms; state ≠ capability ≠ service ≠ resilience ≠ sustainability; two sustainability pathways and measured SDG-only mapping.
6. **Style governance:** Use white slide backgrounds/panel interiors, authored 13 approved Deck3 sRGB tokens, small ASU Gold institutional accents; natural equipment colors for authentic photos. Use Times New Roman for thesis-authored content as specified by current Deck3; this is **not** a claim that Times New Roman is ASU's official default office font.
7. **Release:** Verify slide count, visually inspect every slide at live display size, test editability, check accurate adjacent citations and source provenance, and report any remaining unrun Google/PPTX accessibility and scientific checks. The Google link is the live deck; exported PPTX/PDF are dated derivative snapshots.

## Scope and activation

This is a **governance/source template reference and delivered deck pointer**, not a new research objective, automatic data sync, approved ASU endorsement or global requirement that all non-ASU projects adopt ASU styles. Update Deck3 dispatcher, workflow, machine registry, root instructions and presentation-related companion skills using the repository's global change contract.
